title: Arbor Finance - Procurement: MSA/DPA/SLA Review & Onboarding
summary: Procurement and legal review of Redwood MSA/DPA/SLA. Arbor asked clarifying questions on data residency, KMS/CMK support, SOC 2/ISO attestations, breach notification timelines, audit of subprocessors, liability caps, and termination/data return. Redwood committed to send redlined MSA/DPA, SOC 2 Type II attestation, Dedicated pricing and pilot SOW. Target decision timeline: procurement to finalize by 2027-09-20; pilot targeted mid-October.
action_items: Liam Chen: Send redlined MSA and updated DPA by 2027-09-13
Priya Patel: Share SOC 2 Type II report, ISO references, and security whitepaper by 2027-09-11
Noah Rivera: Provide onboarding plan and 2-week pilot SOW by 2027-09-14
Maya Singh (Arbor): Review redlines and confirm legal exceptions by 2027-09-20
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA and DPA
Redwood to attach SOC2 Type II report and KMS/HSM integration docs
Redwood to provide Dedicated capacity pricing sheet and pilot SOW
Schedule SE-led technical onboarding call next week to scope pilot
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-09 10:00 AM PT - Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Rivera (Redwood CSM), Daniel Reed (Arbor Procurement), Maya Singh (Arbor Legal), Carlos Mendez (Arbor CISO), Anika Patel (Arbor CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Platform Eng)

00:00 Liam Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, I'm Liam from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer and Noah from customer success. we'll run through the MSA/DPA questions and then Priya can take the tech bits.
00:18 Daniel Reed: Great, thanks Liam. We got the MSA and DPA, quick note - procurement is looking for any redlines that are non-starter, and a timeline for onboarding, and cost for dedicated vs hosted.
00:30 Liam Chen: Totally, high level we support hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and a private VPC option. For enterprise customers like Arbor we typically recommend dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation, but we can scope pilot on hosted if you want faster time to value.
00:47 Maya Singh: On the DPA specifically, we need to confirm data residency for EU customers and whether we can get subprocessor lists and 30-day breach notification.
01:05 Priya Patel: Yep - we have region pinning, Redwood has EU regions and we can commit to processing in region when you pin that in the tenant settings. subprocessors list we can share, and standard breach notification is 72 hours but we can discuss contractual language.
01:25 Carlos Mendez: 72 hours is pretty standard, but we need clarity on root cause analysis timeline and whether logs/audit trails are available for 90 days. Also KMS integration - we want customer-managed keys (CMK) via our KMS/HSM.
01:45 Priya Patel: We support customer-managed keys, integrate with major KMS providers and HSMs; there are a couple implementation patterns - bring-your-own-key via our KMS connector, or use our HSM-based envelope encryption. Audit logs are available, and we can set retention to 90 days in the console or export to your SIEM.
02:10 Anika Patel: From a platform perspective, what's the network setup for Private deployment? We need VPC peering or private link, and also the latency numbers - we have sub-millisecond SLA needs for some scoring calls.
02:30 Priya Patel: Private deployment can be VPC-hosted with private link and dedicated host nodes. Latency depends on model, sequence length and GPU type; for smaller models on A100-type infra we've seen p50 latencies in 50-80ms for single-turn generation, larger models higher. For strict low-lat SLOs we can do colocated edge pools.
03:00 Daniel Reed: Pricing - procurement wants an annual committed quote for Dedicated, and also a pilot PO to get the pilot started. We need the pricing sheet and any ramp discounts.
03:18 Liam Chen: We'll follow up with a detailed pricing sheet for Dedicated with commit tiers and expected unit pricing, plus a separate pilot quote that can be converted to committed capacity.
03:32 Maya Singh: A couple legal points - indemnity carve-outs for third-party claims, data return/secure deletion at termination, and the ability to audit subprocessors. Also, can you confirm you have SOC 2 Type II?
03:50 Noah Rivera: We do - Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO references, we'll attach the attestation and security whitepaper. For audits of subprocessors we can provide SSAE reports and a process for reasonable audits, subject to redaction and non-disclosure.
04:20 Carlos Mendez: On SLAs, we need to define uptime, latency SLOs and credits. Also escalation path and on-call details.
04:36 Liam Chen: Our standard enterprise SLA includes 99.9% uptime for Dedicated control plane and an SLO for p95 latency targets per model type; credits are tiered. We'll share the SLA doc with explicit credit calculations and escalation contacts.
05:00 Maya Singh: Termination for convenience clause - can we get data export assistance and secure wipe within 30 days?
05:12 Priya Patel: Yes we provide export tools and a secure deletion workflow. For Private deployments we can also provide a facility for on-prem wipe. We usually agree to 30-day assisted export and deletion, we'll include language in the redline.
05:28 Daniel Reed: Good. One more - liability cap. Our legal team wants to understand the standard cap and exceptions for gross negligence.
05:40 Liam Chen: Our baseline is market standard; we'll surface the exact language in the redline but we can discuss reasonable exceptions for indemnity around IP claims and will work with you on specifics.
05:52 Anika Patel: How do you handle model updates and rollbacks? We need predictable behavior if a model update regresses accuracy for critical paths.
06:08 Priya Patel: We have rollout policies, canary deploys, and we support model version pinning. Also quality monitoring tied to eval prompt sets - we can setup regression alerts and automatic rollback to previous model on deviation.
06:30 Sofia Alvarez: For the pilot, we need a clear scope: sample volume, endpoints, expected latency, and success criteria. Can you propose a 2-week pilot SOW?
06:45 Noah Rivera: Absolutely - we'll propose a 2-week pilot SOW: 2 models, up to 100k tokens/day, dedicated small pool or hosted with reserved throughput, telemetry and cost breakdown, and a joint success criteria doc.
07:05 Daniel Reed: Also procurement needs the MSA redlines in track changes so Legal can review them next week.
07:15 Liam Chen: We'll send the redline by Monday EOD (redline target: 2027-09-13).
07:23 Maya Singh: We might need an exception for data retention for certain regulated customers, will note in review.
07:35 Priya Patel: Yep we can make that configurable per-tenant and include options in the SOW.
07:50 Daniel Reed: Any concerns about our use case? We're doing KYC scoring and PII handling - want to make sure DPA covers the flows.
08:02 Carlos Mendez: also need to confirm we can restrict persistence of PII in model training/updates.
08:15 Priya Patel: Redwood's hosted models are not used to retrain on customer data by default; we have clear data isolation policies and options to opt-out of telemetry collection. For Private deployments data never leaves your environment unless you enable it.
08:40 Daniel Reed: Good. Competitors - we evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic and did some benchmarks, Redwood's performance numbers looked promising but procurement wants to validate cost delta for Dedicated.
09:00 Liam Chen: Understood, we'll include a cost comparison sheet and expected per-token/unit economics for your workloads.
09:12 Maya Singh: Ok last question: will you accept our standard security questionnaire?
09:22 Noah Rivera: Yes please send it over; we'll assign it to our security team and get back with answers within 3 business days.
09:33 Daniel Reed: Perfect. Next steps?
09:36 Liam Chen: Recap: Redwood sends redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2 attestation, Dedicated pricing, pilot SOW and onboarding plan. Arbor to review legal redlines and return notes by 2027-09-20. Schedule the SE technical onboarding next week - Priya will lead.
09:56 Maya Singh: Thanks everyone, we'll look for the redlines and security docs.
10:00 Liam Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and Slack, talk soon.

Note: Some transcription noise - speaker labels occasionally overlap and a couple of technical terms were transcribed as k V cache vs KV cache, also references to VPC may have been captured as V P C.
